tasks.title: FIELD STOP 1: Mueang Sing Historic Park
tasks.statement:
Location: Mueang Sing Historic Park, Sai Yok District, Kanchanaburi Province (UTM Grid, 526329E/1552087N, 14 02 21.5 N/99 14 37.9 E)

FIELD INFO: Group 1-4 will conduct fieldwork at this site. There are 3 stops and time allocation for each stop is 1 hour. Group 1-2 will work at stop A, group 3 at stop B, and group 4 at stop C. After one hour of work, each group has to rotate as guided by our volunteer.

Background: The historical park was built on the floodplain of the Kwae Noi River. The Muang Sing / Prasat Muang Sing Temple is an ancient Khmer Bayon-style temple. The history of the site goes back to the period between 867 and 1157 A.D., a period when the Khmer Kingdom flourished. The area was declared as a historical site by the Fine Arts Department, Ministry of Culture, Government of Thailand in 1987 (Figures 1 & 2).

Research: 
1. Did the rocks here at stop A and stop C form in situ?
2. What earth system interrelationship do these rocks present?

parts.question: Conduct fieldwork at Stop A, B, and C, identify rocks, describe characteristics and phenomena, test hypotheses, and answer research questions about earth system interrelationships.

tasks.title: FIELD STOP 2: Death Railway and Krasae Cave
tasks.statement:
Location: Death Railway and Krasae Cave, Sai Yok District, Kanchanaburi Province (UTM Grid, 518079E/1559395N, 14 06 19.6 N/99 10 02.4 E)

The Krasae Cave is located on the western bank of the meandering Kwae Noi River, along a segment of the Three Pagodas Fault escarpment and the Death Railway in Sai Yok District.

FIELD INFO: Group 5-7 will conduct fieldwork at this site. There are 2 stops and time allocation for each stop is 1 hour 30 minutes. Group 5 will work at stop A, and group 6-7 at stop B. After one hour and a half of work, each group has to rotate as guided by our volunteer.

Background: Krasae Cave is a small one-sided open cave approximately 6-8 * 16-20 m in size. The Death Railway, situated abreast of the cave, was built during World War II (1939-1945) with the minimum supply of construction equipment but mainly by construction tools and human labor.

Research:
What kind of earth system interrelationship are presented by this cave?

parts.question: Identify rocks in and around the cave and escarpment, describe phenomena explaining the cave history, observe river levels before and after dam construction, and assess geohazards.

tasks.title: FIELD STOP 3: Sai Yok Noi Waterfall
tasks.statement:
Location: The Sai Yok Noi Waterfall is located in the Tha Sao Village, Sai Yok District of Kanchanaburi. (UTM Grid. 506194E/1574153N)

Background: The Sai Yok Noi Waterfall is a popular tourist attraction. The area has been known for its natural beauty for a long time, perhaps at least since the reign of King Rama V (1868-1910 AD).

FIELD INFO: Group 8-11 will conduct fieldwork at this site. There are 2 stops and time allocation for each stop is 1 hour plus moving from Stop A to Stop B and vice versa for 30 minutes. Group 8-9 work at stop A while group 10-11 work at stop B. After one hour of work, each group has to rotate as guided by our volunteer.

Research:
1. What kind of earth system interrelationship are presented by this waterfall?

parts.question: Identify rock at the cliff, observe waterfall history phenomena, collect water samples from the river at both stops, and measure chemical and physical parameters (T, pH, salinity, carbonate, bicarbonate, nitrate, DO).

tasks.title: FIELD STOP 4: Wang Krachae Hotspring
tasks.statement:
Location: Wang Krachae Hotspring is located at Wang Krachae Subdistrict, Sai Yok District, Kanchanaburi Province. (UTM Grid, 503185E/1570861N)

FIELD INFO: Group 12-15 will conduct fieldwork at this site. There are 3 stops and time allocation for each stop is 1 hour. Group 12-13 work at stop A, group 14 work at stop B, and group 15 work at stop C. After one hour of work, each group has to rotate as guided by our volunteer.

Research:
1. What kind of earth system interrelationship are presented by this waterfall?

parts.question: Observe and describe hotspring phenomena, measure flow rate, collect water samples and measure parameters, calculate reservoir temperature using geothermometer equations, examine geosphere-biosphere interrelationships at Stop B, and investigate the abandoned hotspring spa pool at Stop C.

tasks.title: FIELD STOP 5: Kwae Noi River Section
tasks.statement:
Location: This section of Kwae Noi River is located at Tha Sao Subdistrict, Sai Yok District, Kanchanaburi Province.

FIELD INFO: Group 16-18 will conduct fieldwork at this site. There are 2 stops and time allocation for each stop is 1 hour 30 minutes. Group 16-17 work at stop A, and group 18 work at stop B. After one hour and ten minutes of work, each group has to rotate as guided by our volunteer.

Research:
1. What kind of earth system interrelationship are presented by the data of the Kwae Noi River that were collected (directly and indirectly)?

parts.question: Identify river bank sediment characteristics, observe geohazards, calculate river flow velocity and rate of river flow at the bridge given geometric and transit time data, and collect water samples for parameter measurement.

tasks.title: ESSAY PROBLEM: Land Subsidence in Bangkok Metropolitan Area
tasks.statement:
The Bangkok metropoli area has an estimated population of close to 20 million due to its geographic location on the lower Chao Phraya River Plain as well as its political location as the capital city of Thailand. Geologically, however, the city is located on very thick deposit of of Bangkok clay and interbedded with river sand and hard clay of > 2 km thickness before reaching the bedrock of granite and metamorphic rock. Overpumping of the ground water for domestic consumption from more than 8 artesian aquifer within the Bangkok Metropoli and surrounding area, namely, Sam Prakarn, Sam Sakorn, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani, and Ayuthaya has resulted in extensive land subsidence in the lower central plain. The maximum subsidence of >2 m was measured for the northern part of Bangkok in early 2002 to 2005 and large area of Bangkok and Sam prakarn were below mean sea level already. Drastic measure had been taken, including prohibition of ground water pumping in Bangkok, Samrakarn, Nonthaburi, and Pathum Thani. By that time, a large chunk of the Bangkok Metropoli had already subsided below mean sea level. Bangkok Metropoli and Nonthaburi had to build concrete embankment on both side of the river to protect the city from perpetual flooding. At the same time, the Bangkok Municipality Office has enacted regulation that required all new houses in the Metropoli to raise the land above mean sea level before construction permits were issued. Furthermore, a water intrusion into the first artesian aquifer beneath the city has occurred. For namely, by that time the ground water level in the depleted aquifer is gradually rising; thus ground water recharge is unwarranted.

Student of each team are asked to research this problem. At least four aspects related to soil subsidence need to be presented. Also, propose method to mitigate this problem.

parts.question: Research the land subsidence problem in Bangkok, present at least four aspects related to soil subsidence, and propose methods to mitigate the problem.
